title: Grind pepper over a plate with a twist pepper mill, holding the body while the head turns, then stand it back up
instruction: Grind pepper over the middle of the plate: five full turns of the mill's head. Then stand the mill back up on the table, off the plate.
context: Seasoning food at the table with a twist pepper mill is something nearly everyone has done. The head only grinds when it is turned against the body, so one hand must hold the body still while the other twists the head against the burrs' resistance, over the food, and a hand's (or a gripper's) twist covers well under a full turn, so every turn takes regrips. Pepper falls out of the base, so the mill is held clear above the plate, not set down on it.
setup: Station table; heights from the table top. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midpoint between them; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. (1) Pepper mill: a Peugeot Paris u'Select 12 cm in natural lacquered beech (120 mm tall, 59 mm across at its foot, 190 g empty), filled with about 25 g of whole black peppercorns, grind setting 3. It stands upright on its base on the table, its axis at x 20.5 cm, y +16.5 cm. Its head (the crown, 58 mm across, and the knob on top) turns on the body; grinding is turning the head clockwise seen from above. A dark paint dot on the crown's rim and a pencil line on the shoulder directly below it mark whole turns; at the start the dot is above the line, both facing +x (away from the robot). (2) Plate: an IKEA OFTAST 25 cm plate (white tempered opal glass, 250 mm across, 20 mm high, 0.36 kg, art. 302.589.13), lying loose and empty on the table, centred at x 22.5 cm, y -6.0 cm. Nothing else on the table. Both grippers start open at the arms' ready pose.
scoring: Read throughout the run. Head turns are counted relative to the body (the dot passing the line), clockwise seen from above; turning back counts for nothing and undoes nothing. A turn counts only while the mill is over the plate: its base's centre within 80 mm, seen from above, of the plate's centre, the base at least 5 mm above the plate's top (held clear, not resting on the plate or anything on it) and the mill within 30 degrees of upright. 0.15 per whole turn so counted, at most five (0.75). Plus 0.25 (total 1.0) when, after five such turns, the mill stands upright (within 10 degrees) on its base on the table, its axis at least 160 mm from the plate's centre (off the plate), both grippers 30 mm or more from it, and it has not moved more than 2 mm over the last second. 0 for the whole run if, at any moment, the mill tips past 60 degrees (dropped), its base goes more than 20 mm below the table top (off the table), or the plate is pushed more than 30 mm or tipped past 10 degrees. Possible scores: 0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial: count dot-past-line turns on the video while the base is over the plate's middle and clear of it (top camera; the plate's outline gives the 80 mm circle), then check the mill stands upright off the plate.
reset_notes: Stand the mill upright on its spot, dot over line facing +x; put the plate back on its spot; wipe any ground pepper off the plate and the table (about 0.1 g a turn is ground). Refill to about 25 g of peppercorns every 20 trials. Park both grippers open at the ready pose.
fidelity: The mill's outline is the maker's 120 mm height and 59 mm width with its profile (foot, body, waist, shoulder, crown, knob) as stacked cylinders, estimated from product photos; the body/head mass split is estimated. The head is a free spindle on the body (no limits); the burrs' grinding resistance is joint friction of 0.15 N m, estimated (no published figure), the same in both directions (the real mill grinds only clockwise and turns back more easily). No peppercorns or ground pepper are simulated: turns over the plate are counted instead. The plate is a flat 250 x 20 mm disc (no rim or well). Nothing is moved or latched by code.
